title: The work package is labelled (E1-018) while the source worked example is story RWB-E1-020
source: WP C-WEX heading 'Worked Example next version (E1-018)'; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Story Worked Example v6.md metadata 'Story key | RWB-E1-020'; _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json legacy RWB-E1-020 (primary P3, 7 slices)
section: Front matter; s1 Story; s18 Traceability
description: The work package that produces this version names E1-018 in its heading, but the only source it gives is the worked example of RWB-E1-020 (allocation and assignment engine). E1-018 is a different legacy story in the same service (case ID issuance and case record), with its own slice set RWB-P3-E1018-CON, RWB-P3-E1018-APP, RWB-P3-E1018-OPS, RWB-P5-E1018-APP, RWB-P1-E1018-APP, RWB-P4-E1018-APP, RWB-P7-E1018-APP and RWB-ITG-E1018-ITG. No source says whether the work package means to convert the E1-020 example or to replace it with an E1-018 example, and the two would produce different documents.
evidence: WP C-WEX line 1: '# WP C-WEX - Worked Example next version (E1-018)'; WP C-WEX line 4 names only '04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Story Worked Example v6.md'; that file line 9: '| Story key | RWB-E1-020 |'; _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json legacy entries for RWB-E1-018 and RWB-E1-020 both exist as separate keys.
proposed: Read the '(E1-018)' in the work package heading as a scheduling label and keep RWB-E1-020 as the subject of the document, because the source file, every identifier in it and the split plan all belong to RWB-E1-020; note the reading in the edit log of the run and correct the heading in the work package index of the next run.

title: No source names the rwb-case database login or where the caseload cap is stored
source: Template and Rules R4 (one login per service, schema rwb_<name>) and R5.5 DP-02 and DP-06; legacy story RWB-E1-020 section 3 (service identity SY-CASEWF, rules identity SY-RULES) and section 11 (queue.capacity_cap, queue_member.capacity); Ownership Map v1 table rows for recovery_case, queue, queue_member, assignment, parameter_catalog, parameter_value
section: s3 Preconditions; s8 Business rules BR3; s11 Data; s13 Solution plan
description: The target gives every service its own database login, but no source states the login name of rwb-case. The legacy story names the shared monolith logins recovery_svc, SY-CASEWF and SY-RULES, which the target retires. The caseload cap is the same kind of gap: the legacy story reads 150 from queue.capacity_cap and queue_member.capacity, while DP-06 routes configuration through the rwb-case parameter contract, and no source says whether the cap stays a queue column, becomes a parameter row, or both.
evidence: Template and Rules R4: 'login per service' with no name; DP-02: 'recovery_svc login -> One login per service'; legacy RWB-E1-020 section 3: 'The job runs as service identity SY-CASEWF; rules are evaluated as SY-RULES'; section 11: 'DF-WRK-007 | queue | capacity_cap | Read'; Ownership Map v1: parameter_catalog and parameter_value are P3 rwb-case tables, and queue and queue_member are P3 rwb-case tables, so both options are owned by the same service.
proposed: Publish the per-service login in RWB-PLT-DB and in the rwb-case DB story rather than in this story, and keep the placeholder here; keep the cap as data on the queue (queue.capacity_cap and queue_member.capacity) with the default delivered through the parameter contract, so that no value is written in code either way.

title: The schedule expression of the DailyCaseRun (legacy JOB-03) is not stated by any source
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-020 section 12 (Trigger: Quartz, after JOB-02 completes; Schedule: daily after JOB-02, complete by 07:00 Asia/Bangkok); Arch v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44 (JOB-03 owner rwb-case) and the P3 contract line 'DailyCaseRun (Schedule + AceDataReady)'; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 (Schedules replace Quartz)
description: The legacy trigger was a Quartz cron after JOB-02, with a 07:00 deadline. The target replaces it with a Temporal Schedule plus an event start on AceDataReady, but no source gives the Temporal cron expression, the timezone handling, or the rule for a business date that has no run. The 07:00 deadline and the dependency on the ACE business date are stated; the expression that produces the run is not.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-020 section 12: 'Trigger | Quartz, after JOB-02 completes for the business date' and 'Schedule | Daily after JOB-02, complete by 07:00 Asia/Bangkok'; Arch v5 Text Extract v1: 'DailyCaseRun (Schedule + AceDataReady)'; no file in the read set carries a cron string for the run.
proposed: Keep the event start on AceDataReady as the primary trigger and register one catch-up Schedule per business date with overlap policy SKIP; fix the cron expression in RWB-P3-E1020-OPS where the deployment is described, and keep 07:00 Asia/Bangkok as the deadline the alert measures.

title: No single source divides the thirteen legacy criteria of RWB-E1-020 across its seven stories
source: _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json legacy RWB-E1-020 (seven slices, no acceptance criterion listed per slice); _work/msr/plan/legacy_index.json (ACS AC1 to AC13, TCS TC-E1-020-01 to TC-E1-020-15); the seven story files of the family, each claiming its own criteria; _work/msr/extract/C-EPICS/Recovery Workbench Service Story Catalog v1.md
section: s5 Exception paths X7; s7 Acceptance criteria (note under the block); s16 Test cases; s18 Traceability
description: The legacy story has thirteen criteria and fifteen test cases. The target spreads them over a contract story, an app story, a deployment story and three secondary service stories plus an integration story, and the split plan records only the slice list. Each story file states its own set, so the sets agree only if the reader compares them; no register holds the division. The same is true of the legacy test cases: fourteen stay with the app story and TC-E1-020-10 is executed by RWB-P3-E1018-APP, but no source states that rule.
evidence: split_plan.json: '"RWB-E1-020": { ..., "slices": ["RWB-P3-E1020-CON", "RWB-P3-E1020-APP", ... ] }' with no acs key; legacy_index.json: '"acs": ["AC1" ... "AC13"], "tcs": ["TC-E1-020-14" ...]'; RWB-P3-E1020-APP section 19: 'AC10 of the legacy story ... is owned by RWB-P3-E1018-APP'; RWB-ITG-E1020-ITG section 16: 'TC-E1-020-10-ITG is the copy this story signs off'.
proposed: Add one criterion-ownership column to the Legacy map sheet of the Service Story Catalog v1, listing for each legacy criterion the single new story that owns it, and take the division stated by the story files as the record until then.
